purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Look at what I changed a few minutes ago
finding: Every row in the 'All changes' list carries a clickable timestamp labelled 'Jump to 14:32'. Clicking it does not jump or preview — it RESTORES, and the restore permanently truncates history: everything recorded after that point is deleted from the stack and the redo stack is emptied. There is no confirm, no toast, and no way back. The word 'Jump' promises navigation and the click performs an irreversible edit. The sibling surface one filter away (Milestones) confirms every restore with a banner that says 'Your current work is saved first — nothing is lost'; this path saves nothing first.
evidence: ActivityView.tsx:360-393 handleTimestampClick -> composer.history.restoreEntry(entryId); aria-label/title at :536-537 read 'Jump to <time>'. HistoryManager.ts:757-775 restoreEntry clears redoStack and does undoStack.slice(0, entry.index + 1). Contrast VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:198-218 handleRestoreClick -> restoreConfirmId -> confirm band at :359-378. Searched: 'restoreEntry', 'handleTimestampClick', 'Jump to', 'confirm'.
fix: Make the timestamp do what it says — preview the state, entering the same preview band the scrubber uses ('Previewing X / Nothing is written until Restore'). Restore stays a separate, confirmed action that states what it discards ('N later changes will be dropped') and, like the Milestones path, saves the current work first.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Scrub back through my session and take the state I want
finding: 'Restore this point' in the Time-Travel drawer fires straight into the same truncating restore with no confirmation, while the identical operation on a named version two clicks away shows a confirm band. A user who scrubs to explore and presses the obvious primary button loses everything after that point without being asked.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:264-268 handleRestore -> onRestore(currentEntry.id); HistoryTab.tsx:195-201 handleScrubberRestore -> composer.history.restoreEntry. HistoryManager.ts:757-775 truncates. Confirmed path in VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:359-378. Searched: 'handleRestore', 'onRestore', 'restoreEntry', 'RESTORE_CONFIRM'.
fix: One restore contract across the module: preview → confirm that names the cost → restore, with the current state auto-saved as a version first. The scrubber's own panel band already says 'Nothing is written until Restore' — make the button honour it.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Search my saves while the scrubber is open
finding: The scrubber installs a document-level keydown handler with NO guard for text fields. While it is open the History panel still renders its search input directly above. Typing a query and pressing Enter — the universal 'submit my search' gesture — is swallowed by the scrubber and executes 'Restore this point' on whatever the slider happens to be sitting on, which by default is the MIDDLE of the stack. A search keystroke destroys the user's later work.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:270-286 document keydown: 'Enter' && !shift && !ctrl -> preventDefault + handleRestore(); no activeElement/INPUT/TEXTAREA check anywhere in the effect. The search field stays mounted while showScrubber is true — HistoryTab.tsx:272-294 renders it inside the unconditional activeView === 'saves' branch, and the drawer at :378-386 is a sibling. Contrast ActivityView.tsx:268-273, which DOES guard on INPUT/TEXTAREA. Searched: 'activeElement', 'INPUT', 'TEXTAREA', 'e.key === "Enter"'.
fix: Scope the scrubber's keys to the drawer (focus-trapped, since it already claims aria-modal), or at minimum guard on the focused element the way the sibling list does. Enter should never be a destructive default.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Move the selection on canvas while time-travel is open
finding: The scrubber claims Left/Right arrows at the document level and the canvas claims the same keys for selection navigation and 1px/10px moves. Both fire: the canvas handler runs first (React root), calls preventDefault, and the scrubber's own listener has no defaultPrevented check, so one arrow press both walks the element selection AND steps the timeline. The canvas is still fully interactive because the scrubber's overlay layer is pointer-events:none and its preview layer sits at opacity 0 when it has no snapshot.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:271-275 ArrowLeft/ArrowRight -> preventDefault + updateToIndex, registered on document with no defaultPrevented test. useCanvasKeyboard.ts:78 'if (e.defaultPrevented) return' + :280-300 arrow cases. TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:178 layer.style.pointerEvents='none'; history.css:914-926 .tt-overlay is pointer-events:none until .active. Searched: 'ArrowLeft', 'defaultPrevented', 'pointerEvents', 'nudge'.
fix: Time-travel is a mode, not an overlay — while it is on, the canvas should be non-editable and its keys inert, so arrows unambiguously mean 'step the timeline'. Say so on the canvas, not only in the sidebar band.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Undo something I did a while ago
finding: Undo is capped at 100 steps and the oldest entries are silently discarded — the list simply stops going back, with no line saying where history begins or that anything was dropped. An event for exactly this announcement was declared and never wired: HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING has zero emitters and zero listeners.
evidence: config.ts:108 HISTORY_MAX_SIZE: 100; HistoryManager.ts:626-643 trimHistory() shifts entries off the front with no emit. events.ts:133 declares HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING. Searched all three spellings: 'HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING', 'history:capacity-warning', 'capacityWarning' — the constant declaration is the only hit in src/.
fix: End the list with a stated boundary ('History starts here — earlier steps were dropped') and tell the user, once, when the cap is first hit, with the door to 'Save a version' beside it. The named-version path is the durable answer and nothing points at it at the moment it becomes relevant.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Recover when the change list fails to load
finding: The 'All changes' list has a built error state — an alert, a 'Failed to load activity' title and a Retry button — that no user can ever reach: the parent never passes `error` or `onRetry`. If the underlying read fails the list falls through to the empty state and tells the user they have 'No undo history', which is the same lie the Saves list was explicitly fixed for on its own board ('Your versions are still stored. Only this list failed to load.').
evidence: ActivityView.tsx:643-658 renders the error branch off props `error`/`onRetry`; HistoryTab.tsx:333-341 mounts ActivityView with composer/searchQuery/onOpenTimeTravel/onClearHistory/canClear only — grep for 'error=' and 'onRetry' in HistoryTab.tsx returns nothing. Compare the wired equivalent at VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:290-305. Searched: 'error=', 'onRetry', 'loadError'.
fix: Wire the failure through, or delete the branch. A list that cannot distinguish 'nothing happened' from 'I could not read it' will tell people their work is gone.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Clear my undo history
finding: 'Clear' wipes the entire undo stack. The confirm is the same button re-labelled 'Clear all' with a Cancel beside it — it never states the consequence (undo stops working for everything before this moment, and it is not recoverable). It also lives only inside the 'All changes' filter, so the control that destroys history is hidden behind a filter chip, while the list it destroys is the one feeding the change counts shown on the Milestones filter.
evidence: ActivityView.tsx:334-341 handleClearClick (two-press inline confirm), :407-435 renders 'Clear' -> 'Clear all' / 'Cancel' with no explanatory copy; HistoryTab.tsx:338 onClearHistory={clear} from useHistoryState.ts:25. HistoryManager.ts:783-799 clear() empties both stacks. Searched: 'onClearHistory', 'confirmingClear', 'clear()'.
fix: Either state the cost in the confirm ('Undo will stop working for the 47 steps before now. Saved versions are not affected.') or drop the control — nothing about a session's undo stack needs manual clearing, and the button's only reachable outcome is data loss.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Take my version history with me / move it between projects
finding: The engine can export the whole version history to a file and import one back, including a clear-existing mode. No screen calls either. A user cannot back up, move or restore their saves outside the browser they made them in — and IndexedDB is where they live.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:360-389 exportVersions(download)/importVersions(file, clearExisting); VersionHistoryStorage.ts:269,284 the storage halves. Searched 'exportVersions', 'importVersions', 'VERSION_EXPORTED', 'VERSION_IMPORTED' across src/ — every hit is inside engine/ or its tests; no editor/ caller.
fix: Give Saves an overflow with Export / Import, with import defaulting to merge and naming the destructive option explicitly. If this is deliberately out of scope, delete the engine surface so the next audit does not re-file it.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Find the state I want to go back to
finding: Two fundamentally different things are presented as two filters of one list. 'Milestones' are named versions in persistent storage with a documented retention rule ('50 kept, named ones never prune'). 'All changes' is the in-memory undo stack — capped at 100 and gone on reload. The chips say only 'Milestones' and 'All changes', so a user reasonably reads the second as a superset of the first, saves nothing, reloads, and finds their afternoon gone.
evidence: HistoryTab.tsx:38-41 FILTER_LABEL + :242-253 chip row; :343-356 milestones -> VersionHistoryPanel (persistent, useVersionHistory), :333-341 changes -> ActivityView (useHistoryState.ts:46 composer.history.getHistoryStack, in-memory). SavesChrome.tsx:161-169 prints the retention rule under BOTH filters, which reinforces the misread. Searched: 'savesFilter', 'FILTER_LABEL', 'getHistoryStack', 'maxVersions'.
fix: Name them for what survives: 'Saved versions' vs 'This session'. Put the durability sentence on the session list, not only under the versions list, and offer 'Save this point as a version' from any session row.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Get out of time-travel
finding: The drawer declares itself a modal dialog but has no Escape. The exits are the 'Exit time-travel' button and Ctrl+Shift+T — a chord the browser owns (reopen closed tab) and which the panel's own list handler does not implement as an exit. Escape while the drawer is open is caught by the change list and only collapses an expanded row, so the reflex key does nothing visible and the user is left with a past frame over the canvas.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:315-318 role='dialog' aria-modal='true'; :270-286 the key handler implements ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Enter/Ctrl+Shift+T and no 'Escape' case. ActivityView.tsx:305-310 Escape only clears expandedGroupId/showAllIds/confirmingClear. HistoryTab.tsx:184-193 registers Ctrl+Shift+T as a toggle. Searched: 'Escape', 'onExit', 'aria-modal', 'Ctrl+Shift'.
fix: Escape exits the mode. Pick a chord the browser does not own, and put the exit in the canvas overlay where the user's attention is, not only in a drawer under it.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: See the past state while scrubbing
finding: The drawer's horizontal position is hardcoded to the rail width on the left and a fixed 320px on the right. The History panel it is opened FROM is 280px wide (700px expanded) and sits on top of that left edge, so roughly the first 232px of the drawer — including the start-of-range timestamp — is under the panel. The right inset assumes an inspector that is always exactly 320px and always present.
evidence: history.css:928-934 .tt-drawer { left: var(--bk-space-48); right: 320px; height: 200px }. tokens.generated.css:129 --bk-size-drawer: 280px; LeftSidebar.tsx:586 widens to 700 when expanded. Searched: '.tt-drawer', '--bk-size-drawer', 'panelWidthOverride'.
fix: Anchor the drawer to the canvas region the same way the preview layer already measures #editor-canvas, instead of to two frozen numbers.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Preview an earlier state before restoring
finding: The scrub preview is not a render of the past — it is the nearest NAMED version's screenshot. A user with no named versions (the default: versions are only created by explicit save or auto-checkpoint) gets no image at all: the preview layer is set to opacity 0 and the live canvas shows through unchanged, while the drawer confidently reads 'Previewing: 14:32 — Added block'. The user is looking at the present and being told it is the past, and the button under it restores.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:104-115 renderPreviewForIndex -> findNearestSnapshot(versions, ts)?.visualSnapshot ?? null; :237-241 'else { layer.style.opacity = "0" }'; :131-133 the label prints regardless. The docblock at :5-16 states the tradeoff. Searched: 'visualSnapshot', 'previewSrc', 'findNearestSnapshot'.
fix: When there is no frame for the scrubbed point, say so in the drawer ('No preview for this point — the nearest snapshot is from 13:05') and disable Restore, or fall back to restoring into a preview mode the user can back out of.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Open time-travel
finding: The scrubber opens with the slider parked at the MIDDLE of the stack — an arbitrary past moment — rather than at 'now'. Combined with the unguarded Enter key (UX-I-03) and the invisible preview (UX-I-12), the default position is both meaningless and dangerous.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:74-78 initialIndex = Math.floor(historyStack.length / 2); sliderValue seeded from it. Searched: 'initialIndex', 'currentIndex', 'sliderValue'.
fix: Open at the current state, with the timeline running back from it, so the first thing the user sees matches the canvas.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Mark a moment I might want to come back to
finding: The only control that creates a named, durable restore point is a text link at the foot of the History panel's Milestones filter. It is three navigations from the canvas (open History → Saves → Milestones), has no shortcut, and nothing on the canvas, the topbar or the save flow ever suggests it — while the retention copy elsewhere in the panel promises that named versions are the ones that never prune.
evidence: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:471-482 '+ Save a version' link inside the fab-container; SavesChrome.tsx:161-169 promises 'named ones never prune'. Doors into History: SiteMenu.tsx:198-201 'Version history' and useEditorShortcuts.ts:124-128 Cmd/Ctrl+H. Searched: 'createVersion', 'Save a version', 'forceCheckpoint'.
fix: Put 'Save a version' where the user forms the intent — beside Save in the topbar, and as an action on any session row ('Save this point as a version').

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: Undo a CMS binding or a media delete
finding: Some features deliberately change the project outside history and disable Undo until the next recorded action. The engine announces this on its own event, and nothing in the UI listens — so the only way a user learns that Undo has been switched off is to press Cmd+Z and read a toast telling them it will not work. The switch-off is silent; only the refusal speaks.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:639-646 noteUnrecordedAction -> emit(EVENTS.HISTORY_UNRECORDED); callers BaseBindingManager.ts:106,125,134 and MediaCommandLayer.ts:108. Searched all three spellings — 'HISTORY_UNRECORDED', 'history:unrecorded', 'noteUnrecordedAction' — every src/ hit is the engine or a test; the only UI listener in useHistoryFeedback.ts:254 is HISTORY_NOOP, i.e. the refusal, not the notice.
fix: Reflect the state where the state lives: disable/annotate the undo control the moment history stops covering the last action, and name the action ('Binding a field isn't undoable'). Do not wait for the user to try.

purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
task: See how far the site has drifted since the client approved it
finding: The 'Now — N changes since approval' band and the per-version change counts are both computed from the in-memory undo stack. That stack is capped at 100 entries and reset to a single baseline on every project load, so after a reload the band reads 0 changes on a site that has drifted for days, and the summary line beneath it ('hero copy · 2 images') empties out. A number that resets to zero on refresh is a claim about approval drift that nothing backs.
evidence: SavesChrome.tsx:89-107 counts composer.history.getHistoryStack() filtered by timestamp > approvedAt; VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:273-277 versionChangeCounts(versions, historyStack). HistoryManager.ts:136-157 the PROJECT_LOADED handler resets undoStack/redoStack and records a single 'loaded' checkpoint; :626-643 trims at 100. Searched: 'getHistoryStack', 'approvedAt', 'versionChangeCounts', 'PROJECT_LOADED'.
fix: Derive drift from the persisted versions (or the approved snapshot diff the Compare view already computes), not the session's undo stack. Where the count cannot be known, say 'edited since approval' rather than a number.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Send this site to my client for the first time
finding: Review is the only module with no rail button: its tab config carries no `zone`, and the zone-driven rail render therefore omits it. The reachable doors are the Site menu's 'Review' item, the topbar review pill, the topbar CTA when the next move is a review one, the ReviewBar's Compare link, and the History panel's 'Compare with current' — and every one of the last four exists only once a round already exists (REVIEW_PILL.none is null, ReviewBar returns null with no active round, the approval band only renders when approved). So the FIRST send has exactly one door, buried in an overflow menu, and it is not the one users look in. In the standalone demo at :5050 the same is true — the rail has no Review tab there either.
evidence: tabsConfig.ts:231-244 — the review entry has section/pattern/shortcut/mode but no `zone`, with the comment 'No `zone` → the zone-driven rail render leaves it out'. SiteMenu.tsx:44-55 documents the same fact and :203 renders the one menu item. StudioHeader.tsx:136-142 REVIEW_PILL none -> null; ReviewBar.tsx:116 returns null unless PENDING/CHANGES_REQUESTED. SavesChrome.tsx:129-138 only renders under isApproved. Searched: 'review' in tabsConfig.ts, 'onOpenReview', 'UI_PANEL_OPEN', 'openLeftPanelToTab("review"'.
fix: Give Review a rail seat, or put 'Send for review' on the primary surface where the intent forms (next to Publish). A feature whose only cold-start door is an overflow menu will read as unbuilt.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Re-send the round from the review bar
finding: The review bar's 'Re-send' calls the shell's resend with no client email. The shell only mints a review token when it is given one, so the new round ships with token: null — the client receives no working link, while the button reports success and the old link is superseded. This is the exact defect the Review panel's own code documents having fixed for itself by passing the round's invitedEmail; the bar was never given the same fix.
evidence: ReviewBar.tsx:104-113 `await onResend()` — no argument; AquibraStudio.tsx:401-421 resendReview(clientEmail?) -> submitForReview(undefined, undefined, clientEmail, snapshotPages) with the comment at :410-417 spelling out the consequence. The corrected caller is ReviewTab.tsx:292-294 `onResend(round?.invitedEmail ?? undefined)` with its own comment at :288-291. Searched: 'onResend', 'resendReview', 'invitedEmail', 'submitForReview'.
fix: One re-send path, owned by the panel, with the bar linking to it — not a second implementation of the same verb that drops the argument that makes it work.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Re-send a round while comments are still open
finding: The same destructive verb ships twice with different safety. In the panel, re-sending with open comments raises an inline confirm that says the client gets a NEW link and the old one stops working immediately. In the bar — which is on screen the entire time a round is live, directly under the topbar — the same button fires straight through with no confirm at all. The safer copy exists; the more prominent control does not use it.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:842-855 onClick -> if (openComments.length > 0 && !round.revoked) setConfirmResend(true), confirm panel at :795-816 with the 'old one stops working immediately' sentence. ReviewBar.tsx:148-159 renders Re-send with only a `resending` disable. Searched: 'confirmResend', 'doResend', 'Re-send'.
fix: Route the bar's button at the panel's confirm, or drop it. Two live affordances for the same irreversible action is exactly the condition the panel's own comment warns about.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Decide what to do about the drift I just found
finding: Compare is read-only and ends nowhere. It shows what changed since approval and offers no next move — no 'Re-send for approval', no 'Publish anyway', no way to mark a change as intended. There is also no conflict state at all: the panel has no notion of 'the client approved v3 while you were editing', so the two sides are always presented as simply different, never as competing.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:146-296 — the toolbar is mode buttons + spacer + count + page Select + refresh, and the body is frames or a change list; no action anywhere. ReviewTab.tsx:498-540 wraps it with a Back button and nothing else. Searched 'conflict', 'Conflict', 'CONFLICT' across sidebar/tabs/review and panels/version-history — zero occurrences; 'Review both' — zero occurrences in src/.
fix: End Compare on a decision: 'Send these changes for approval' / 'Publish anyway' / 'Dismiss'. When both sides moved, say so and let the user choose which to keep.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Compare the approved page against the current one
finding: Compare renders two full web pages side by side inside a left-drawer panel whose default width is 280px — about 130px per pane once padding, borders and the gap are taken. The Compare screen also replaces the panel header entirely with a two-item toolbar, so while it is open there is no expand control, no close, and no help: the only control that could widen the panel to 700px has been removed from the screen that needs it most. The result is two unreadable thumbnails, a second toolbar stacked under the first, and a title ('Compare with approved') that the inner toolbar then does not repeat.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:498-505 the compareOpen branch returns a Toolbar with a Back Button and a literal span, replacing the PanelHeader used by every other state (:333-341). ApprovedCompareView.tsx:146-185 the inner toolbar has no title; :261-275 the split stage renders two <Frame> iframes at flex-1. tokens.generated.css:129 --bk-size-drawer: 280px; LeftSidebar.tsx:586 isExpanded -> 700. Searched: 'compareOpen', 'PanelHeader', 'STAGE', '--bk-size-drawer'.
fix: Compare is a full-surface job, not a drawer job — open it on the canvas surface (as Settings already does with mode: fullpage), or at minimum keep the expand control and open it pre-expanded. One header, not two.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Look at the review as a viewer
finding: The panel computes the user's role and uses it in exactly one place — the 'Send for review' control's disabled reason. Resolve, Reopen, Reattach, Revoke link / Withdraw request and Re-send for review are all rendered live and unexplained for a VIEWER, who will click them and get a server rejection with no chrome explaining why. The pattern the codebase already uses (a named disabled reason) exists two lines away.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:146 `const isViewer = useEditorRole() === "VIEWER"` — grep for 'isViewer' in the file returns exactly three hits: :146, :479 and :885, both of the latter being SendForReview's disabledReason. resolveButton at :558-562, revoke at :899-907, re-send at :842-855 carry no role check. Searched: 'isViewer', 'useEditorRole', 'disabledReason', 'readOnlyReason'.
fix: Apply the same named-reason treatment to every mutating control in the panel. A control that is live for someone who cannot use it is worse than one that is visibly shut.

screen: Topbar pill / Review bar / Review panel
purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Understand where my review stands
finding: One state — sent, nothing back — is named three different ways on three surfaces the user sees at once. The topbar pill says 'In review' or 'Opened · no reply'. The bar directly beneath it says 'Sent — waiting on your client'. The panel below that says '<Reviewer> has not commented yet. You will be notified.' Nothing reconciles them, and 'Opened · no reply' is derived from a field ('openedAt') that the review status enum does not even have a value for, so the pill can claim the client opened the link while the bar and panel say only that it was sent.
evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:136-142 REVIEW_PILL table incl. 'opened-not-acted': 'Opened · no reply'. ReviewBar.tsx:126-132 the three-way expression: count>0 -> 'N open', CHANGES_REQUESTED -> 'Changes requested — nothing left open', else 'Sent — waiting on your client'. ReviewTab.tsx:626-634 emptyBody. ReviewBar.tsx:46-49 records that the DB enum is PENDING|APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUESTED with no OPENED. Searched: 'opened-not-acted', 'waiting on your client', 'nothing left open', '0 open'.
fix: One vocabulary, defined once and consumed by all three surfaces, with the pill as the short form of the sentence the bar prints. If 'opened' is a real distinction, it needs to appear in the panel too; if it is not, drop it.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Decide whether to publish over an old approval
finding: There are two independent answers to 'what changed since approval'. The publish gate computes its own page-level diff and lists page names with a bare 'edited / added / removed' — no visual, no detail, capped at six with 'and N more'. The Review panel's Compare computes a typed, itemised diff with side-by-side and overlay rendering. The gate is the moment the user actually has to decide, and it shows the weaker of the two and offers no door to the stronger one.
evidence: StaleApprovalModal.tsx:38-50 its own diffPages(); :162-181 renders page-name rows; the footer offers 'Re-send for approval' / 'Publish anyway' and no Compare. ApprovedCompareView.tsx:113-116 uses compareApprovedToCurrent from @/shared/utils/html with five typed change kinds. Searched: 'diffPages', 'compareApprovedToCurrent', 'StaleApproval', 'Compare'.
fix: One diff, one component. Put 'See what changed' in the gate and open the real Compare; delete the second implementation.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Look at what happened in an earlier round
finding: Opening the round strip lists previous rounds as plain text lines — 'Round 2 · Changes requested · 14/08'. They are spans, not controls: there is no way to open a round, read its comments, or see what was sent. A user who came here to answer 'what did they ask for last time' gets a list of outcomes and stops.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:757-790 — each row is a <span> with a testid; no onClick anywhere in the block. The docblock at :743-747 states the data limit: comments carry no round id, so an older round's comments are not retrievable. Searched: 'roundsOpen', 'review-round-', 'fetchRounds'.
fix: Either make the strip honest about being a log (label it 'Round history' and stop it looking like a list of destinations), or carry the round id on comments so a round can be opened. Right now it reads as broken navigation.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Answer one specific comment
finding: The panel groups comments by page and resolves them individually, but there is exactly one reply box, at the bottom, which posts against a page derived from the FIRST comment in the list. A user answering the third comment on a different page has no way to attach the reply to it — and the helper text says only 'Replies are internal notes on the thread', which does not tell them which thread.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:242 `const activePage = round && comments[0]?.pageId ? comments[0].pageId : undefined`; :244-258 send() -> postReply(body, activePage); the composer at :793-812 is a single Textarea outside every group. Individual rows carry only Resolve/Reopen (:558-562) and Reattach (:700-710). Searched: 'postReply', 'activePage', 'CommentRow', 'actions='.
fix: Reply per comment, inline on the row, the way the resolve action already is. One global box over a grouped list will attach answers to the wrong question.

purpose: Get a client to review the site, collect and resolve their comments, and prove what changed since they approved.
task: Go to the thing that changed
finding: List mode names every change ('Added', 'Removed', 'Content', with a label and a detail line) and none of them is clickable. Having found that a section was removed from /pricing, the user has to leave Compare, switch page and find it by eye. The rows are plain divs.

purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.

So the same bar reading '0 unsaved' means 'nothing typed' on one screen and 'already committed to the server' on another, and the user has no way to tell which kind of screen they are on. The counter is also always 0 or 1 — it says '1 unsaved' whether the user changed one field or twelve.

Redirects, Headers, Localization, Domains, Forms and Webhooks write straight to the server and are invisible to both. purpose: Three recovery-and-configuration modules: keep the user able to go back, get a client's sign-off on what they see, and configure the site as a whole.
task: All three lanes
finding: PURPOSE. History & Versions is the recovery module: it holds the session's undo stack, named/auto version snapshots, a time-travel scrubber, and the published-deploy list — its job is 'put it back the way it was'. Review & Collaboration is the sign-off module: send a client a link, collect and resolve their pinned comments, run rounds, and prove what changed since they approved. Settings is site-wide configuration: identity, SEO, domains, redirects, headers, forms, integrations, webhooks, localization, custom code. PRIMARY TASKS. History: undo/redo; find and restore an earlier state; name a restore point; see what changed since approval; roll back a deploy. Review: send for review (first time and re-send); read and resolve comments; walk the open comments on canvas; compare current against approved; revoke or withdraw. Settings: find a setting; edit it; save or discard; delete a rule/record; upgrade past a plan gate. ENTRY POINTS. History: rail tab 'History' (280px drawer, shortcut H), Cmd/Ctrl+H, Site menu 'Version history' and 'Publish history' (deep-links to the Published view). Review has NO rail seat — Site menu 'Review', the topbar review pill (absent in state 'none'), the topbar next-move CTA, the ReviewBar's Compare, the History approval band's 'Compare with current', and the onboarding checklist; the first send has effectively one door. Settings: rail tab 'Settings' (full-page, shortcut S) — but Cmd+, and Site menu 'Site settings' open a DIFFERENT surface, the project-settings modal. EXIT POINTS. History: panel close / rail toggle; the Time-Travel drawer exits only via its own button or Ctrl+Shift+T (no Escape). Review: panel close, and inside Compare only 'Back', which strands a user who arrived from History. Settings: header ✕ (dirty-guarded), drill-in back, Escape at section level; workspace rows leave for the dashboard in a new tab. HANDOFFS. History receives review state (approval band reads reviews.status) and publish state (PublishHistory + rollback jobs), and hands off to Review (Compare) and to the canvas (restore replaces the element tree, then re-resolves selection). Review receives from the canvas comment layer (orphaned pins, reattach), from the shell (page export for Compare, re-send), and hands off to Publish (the stale-approval gate blocks publishing) and to the canvas (Next › selects a comment's anchor). Settings hands off to Palette/Design system (Branding), to the exporter modal, to the dashboard (Members, Billing), and — for four of its thirteen sections only — into the composer, and therefore into History. The single biggest cross-module gap in this lane is that last one: version history covers only the composer-backed half of Settings, while the restore confirm promises 'nothing is lost'.
evidence: tabsConfig.ts:216-244 (history zone 'config', review with no zone), :187-199 (settings mode 'fullpage'); useEditorShortcuts.ts:119-128 (Cmd+, -> project-settings modal, Cmd+H -> history); SiteMenu.tsx:190-212 (the menu group); HistoryTab.tsx:213-388; ReviewTab.tsx:133-919; SettingsTab.tsx:75-92,795-901; AquibraStudio.tsx:366,401-421,505-536; SavesChrome.tsx:129-138; StaleApprovalModal.tsx:63-181. Searched: 'zone', 'openLeftPanelToTab', 'UI_PANEL_OPEN', 'onOpenReview', 'registerSaveHandler'.
fix: Three structural moves, in order: (1) give Review a first-class door and one re-send path; (2) collapse the two site-settings surfaces into one and make its commit model uniform; (3) make one restore contract — preview, confirm that names the cost, restore — and state plainly what a version does and does not cover.
